# Flickering navigation route display (2026-02-04 14:44Z)

_**User**_

when I start the navigation for a split second it seems that another route / direction is being displayed. I have observed that sometimes during navigation then the display of the next navigation point in the navigation overlay text (navigationoverlaykit) is flipping between this "old" route and "new" route.

THis happens reliably when I just open the navigation and then flip the routes around to bring up the navigation overlay and route instructions

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_


Investigating the route flicker. Searching for NavigationOverlayKit and navigation state management code.

        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "    private func updateNavigationOverlayStep() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed,\n              let route,\n              let navigationOverlayViewModel,\n              let location = locationManager.currentLocation else { return }\n        guard let stepIndex = closestStepIndex(for: route, to: location.coordinate) else { return }\n        if stepIndex != lastOverlayStepIndex {\n            navigationOverlayViewModel.update(step: stepIndex)\n            lastOverlayStepIndex = stepIndex\n        }\n        let step = route.steps[stepIndex]\n        if let remainingMeters = step.polyline.remainingDistance(toEndFrom: MKMapPoint(location.coordinate)) {\n            let measurement = Measurement(value: remainingMeters, unit: UnitLength.meters)\n                .converted(to: navigationOverlayUnit())\n            navigationOverlayViewModel.updateRemainingDistance(to: measurement)\n        } else {\n            let fallback = Measurement(value: step.distance, unit: UnitLength.meters)\n                .converted(to: navigationOverlayUnit())\n            navigationOverlayViewModel.updateRemainingDistance(to: fallback)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func closestStepIndex(for route: MKRoute, to coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D) -&gt; Int? {\n        let point = MKMapPoint(coordinate)\n        var bestIndex: Int?\n        var bestDistance: CLLocationDistance = .greatestFiniteMagnitude\n        for (index, step) in route.steps.enumerated() {\n            guard let distance = step.polyline.closestDistance(to: point) else { continue }\n            if distance &lt; bestDistance {\n                bestDistance = distance\n                bestIndex = index\n            }\n        }\n        return bestIndex\n    }\n\n    private func navigationOverlayUnit() -&gt; UnitLength {\n        let usesMetric: Bool\n        if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {\n            ",

        "contents": "    private func formattedDistance(_ meters: CLLocationDistance) -&gt; String {\n        let usesMetric: Bool\n        if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.measurementSystem == .metric\n        } else {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.usesMetricSystem\n        }\n        let value: Double\n        let unit: UnitLength\n        if usesMetric {\n            value = meters / 1000.0\n            unit = .kilometers\n        } else {\n            value = meters / 1609.344\n            unit = .miles\n        }\n        let measurement = Measurement(value: value, unit: unit)\n        let formatter = MeasurementFormatter()\n        formatter.locale = .current\n        formatter.unitStyle = .short\n        formatter.unitOptions = .providedUnit\n        let numberFormatter = NumberFormatter()\n        numberFormatter.maximumFractionDigits = 0\n        numberFormatter.minimumFractionDigits = 0\n        formatter.numberFormatter = numberFormatter\n        return formatter.string(from: measurement)\n    }\n\n    private func transportSymbolName() -&gt; String {\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: return \"figure.walk\"\n        case 2: return \"car\"\n        case 3: return \"tram\"\n        default: return \"car\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed, let route else {\n            navigationOverlayViewModel = nil\n            lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n            return\n        }\n        navigationOverlayViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: navigationOverlayUnit())\n        lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n        updateNavigationOverlayStep()\n    }\n\n    private func updateNavigationOverlayStep() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed,\n              let route,",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 66
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 81
          }
        },
        "contents": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.",
            "lineNumber": 81
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\n\n### 4) Documentation and changelog\n\n- Update &#96;[CHANGELOG.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/CHANGELOG.md)&#96; with the new “navigation instructions overlay in user→device mode”.\n- Update &#96;[APP_FEATURES.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_FEATURES.md)&#96; (and/or &#96;[APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md)&#96; if you want it marketed) with a short note about in-app navigation instructions when routing from the current device to the selected device.\n\n### Key code touchpoints\n\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96;: add overlay view model, show overlay conditionally, update it when route changes, and update instruction step on location changes.\n  - Current route direction toggle and routing logic are already in place and will be reused:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n640:648:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift\n        if isRouteReversed {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n        } else {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n        }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The overlay should only show for “current device → other device” mode (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- NavigationOverlayKit is already added via SPM and available to the app target.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Manual test: start navigation to a device, switch direction to “current device → other device”, confirm overlay appears with instructions and updates as you move.\n- Verify: switch back to device→user hides overlay;         "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * PlaybackSpeedOverlay.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2026-01-05.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n/// A centered overlay that briefly displays the current playback speed.\nstruct PlaybackSpeedOverlay: View {\n    let speed: Double\n\n    var body: some View {\n        VStack(spacing: 8) {\n            Image(systemName: speed &gt; 1.0 ? \"forward.fill\" : \"play.fill\")\n                .font(.system(size: 28, weight: .semibold))\n                .foregroundStyle(.primary)\n\n            Text(String(format: NSLocalizedString(\"playback_speed_format\", comment: \"Playback speed indicator format like 1x or 2x\"), speed))\n                .font(.system(size: 24, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))\n                .foregroundStyle(.primary)\n        }\n        .padding(.horizontal, 32)\n        .padding(.vertical, 24)\n        .background {\n            if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {\n                Color.clear\n                    .glassEffect(in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))\n            } else {\n                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)\n                    .fill(.ultraThinMaterial)\n                    .overlay(\n                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)\n                            .fill(Color.black.opacity(0.4))\n                    )\n            }\n        }\n        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 16, x: 0, y: 8)\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    ZStack {\n        Color.gray.opacity(0.3)\n            .ignoresSafeArea()\n\n        PlaybackSpeedOverlay(speed: 2.0)\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/navigation_overlay_mode_a06f0fbb.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},

        },
        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1

Color.green : Color.primary)\n                .symbolEffect(.rotate.clockwise.byLayer, options: .nonRepeating, isActive: isUpdating)\n                .padding(.horizontal, 6)\n                .padding(.vertical, 8)\n                .contentShape(Rectangle())\n                .onTapGesture {\n                    if animationsAllowed {\n                        withAnimation { isUpdating = true }\n                    } else {\n                        isUpdating = true\n                    }\n                    Task {\n                        await fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: true, ignoreRouteCache: true)\n                        if animationsAllowed {\n                            withAnimation { isUpdating = false }\n                        } else {\n                            isUpdating = false\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                .onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.6) {\n                    // Toggle global setting for automatic route updates while navigating\n                    settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation.toggle()\n                    isAutoRouteUpdateLocked = settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation\n                    if settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation {\n                        Haptic.notifySuccess()\n                        calculateRoute()\n                    } else {\n                        Haptic.notifyWarning()\n                    }\n                }\n                .accessibilityLabel(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload\", comment: \"Reload target device location\")))\n                .accessibilityHint(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload_longpress_hint\", comment: \"Long-press to toggle automatic route updates.\")))\n        }\n        .animation(animationsAllowed ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : nil, value: isAutoRouteUpdateLocked)\n        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)\n    }",

        "contents": "    private func stopNavigation() {\n        // Stop navigation without dismissing the view\n        // Clear route and navigation info, but keep the map showing both devices\n        route = nil\n        travelTime = nil\n        distanceText = nil\n        navigationOverlayViewModel = nil\n        lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n        routeInfoState.hide()\n        stopAutoUpdate()\n        // Update bottom accessory to reflect that navigation is stopped\n        updateBottomAccessory()\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - Distance Formatting\nextension iPhone_DeviceNavigationView {\n    /// Attempts to reuse a previously calculated route if the movement since that\n    /// calculation was insignificant. Returns true if a cached route was applied\n    /// to the view state, false otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// A cached route is considered valid when BOTH endpoints (user location and\n    /// target device location) have each moved less than the configured threshold since the\n    /// route was stored.         "contents": "    private func useCachedRouteIfValid() -&gt; Bool {\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return false }\n        let transport = settings.navigationTransportType\n        if let cached = routeCache.get(\n            for: self.device.DeviceID,\n            transportType: transport,\n            isRouteReversed: isRouteReversed\n        ) {\n            if routeCache.isValid(\n                cached: cached,\n                currentUserCoordinate: user,\n                currentDeviceCoordinate: device,\n                threshold: routeReuseDistanceThreshold\n            ) {\n                // Apply cached route and keep display fields in sync\n                route = cached.route\n                let formatter = DateComponentsFormatter()\n                formatter.unitsStyle = .short\n                travelTime = formatter.string(from: cached.route.expectedTravelTime)\n                distanceText = formattedDistance(cached.route.distance)\n                refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()\n                // Align last-route inputs so existing change detection logic works\n                lastRouteUserCoordinate = cached.userCoordinate\n                lastRouteDeviceCoordinate = cached.deviceCoordinate\n                lastRouteUserTimestamp = cached.userTimestamp\n                lastRouteDeviceTimestamp = cached.deviceTimestamp\n                lastRouteTransportType = transport\n                return true\n            }\n        }\n        return false\n    }\n    private func formattedDistance(_ meters: CLLocationDistance) -&gt; String {\n        let usesMetric: Bool\n        if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {\n            ",

        "contents": "                    }\n                }\n        }\n        .onChange(of: scenePhase) {\n            switch scenePhase {\n            case .active:\n                LocationManager.shared.appDidEnterForeground()\n            case .background:\n                LocationManager.shared.appDidEnterBackground()\n            default:\n                break\n            }\n        }\n        WindowGroup(for: String.self) { deviceID in\n            DeviceWindowEntrypoint(deviceID: deviceID)\n                .environmentObject(RouteInfoState.shared)\n                .environmentObject(SettingsManager.shared)\n                .animationsGate()\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = url.host ?? \"\"\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow",

---


Logs confirm the issue:

- Line 10: Button tapped (isRouteReversed=true, route exists)
- Line 11: isRouteReversed changed (oldValue=true, newValue=false)
- Line 12: `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` called with isRouteReversed=false but still using the old route (16 steps)
- Line 13: `updateNavigationOverlayStep()` executes with the old route (16 steps)
- Line 17: New route calculated (16 steps)
- Line 18: `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` called again

Root cause: When `isRouteReversed` changes, `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` immediately refreshes using the old route with the new `isRouteReversed` value, causing a brief display of the wrong route.

Fix: When `isRouteReversed` changes, clear the overlay immediately and do not refresh it. Refresh only when the new route is calculated.

Fix applied. Summary:

**Root cause:** When `isRouteReversed` changed, `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` was called immediately with the old route but the new `isRouteReversed` value, causing a brief display of the wrong route.

**Fix:** When `isRouteReversed` changes, the overlay is cleared immediately (set to `nil`) instead of refreshing with stale data. The overlay is refreshed only when the new route is calculated, ensuring it always matches the current route direction.

Verifying the fix:

<reproduction_steps>
1. Build and run the app in Xcode
2. Open navigation for a device
3. Toggle the route direction button (arrow up/down) multiple times to flip routes
4. Verify the navigation overlay text no longer flickers or shows the wrong route
5. Confirm the overlay appears correctly after each route flip
</reproduction_steps>

The logs will show that when `isRouteReversed` changes, the overlay is cleared immediately, and it's only refreshed when the new route arrives. This should eliminate the flickering issue.

        "contents": "        return MKCoordinateRegion(center: center, span: span)\n    }\n\n    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset",

        "contents": "        cache[key] = value\n    }\n\n    func isValid(cached: CachedRoute,\n                 currentUserCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n                 currentDeviceCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n                 threshold: CLLocationDistance? = nil) -&gt; Bool {\n        let limit = threshold ?? defaultDistanceThreshold\n\n        let previousUserLocation = CLLocation(latitude: cached.userCoordinate.latitude,\n                                              longitude: cached.userCoordinate.longitude)\n        let currentUserLocation = CLLocation(latitude: currentUserCoordinate.latitude,\n                                             longitude: currentUserCoordinate.longitude)\n        let userDistance = previousUserLocation.distance(from: currentUserLocation)\n\n        let previousDeviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: cached.deviceCoordinate.latitude,\n                                                longitude: cached.deviceCoordinate.longitude)\n        let currentDeviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: currentDeviceCoordinate.latitude,\n                                               longitude: currentDeviceCoordinate.longitude)\n        let deviceDistance = previousDeviceLocation.distance(from: currentDeviceLocation)\n\n        // Cache is valid only if both ends moved less than the threshold\n        return userDistance &lt; limit &amp;&amp; deviceDistance &lt; limit\n    }\n\n    func clear(for deviceId: String) {\n        cache = cache.filter { $0.key.deviceId != deviceId }\n    }\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/navigation_overlay_mode_a06f0fbb.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 38

        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

The issue: when refreshing the overlay, `updateNavigationOverlayStep()` runs immediately and may select the wrong step (e.g., "Arrive at destination") because the route direction just changed. Adding instrumentation and fixing this:

- [x] H1: When isRouteReversed toggles, refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() is called with old route before new route calculation completes
- [x] H2: updateNavigationOverlayStep() is called during async route calculation using stale route reference
- [ ] H3: Cached route is applied before isRouteReversed state fully propagates, causing overlay to show wrong direction
- [ ] H4: Multiple simultaneous calls to refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() cause overlay to flip between states
- [ ] H5: Location updates trigger updateNavigationOverlayStep() with old route while new route is being calculated
- [x] Fix: Clear overlay immediately when isRouteReversed changes, only refresh when new route arrives
- [-] Fix: When refreshing overlay for new route direction, start at step 0 instead of immediately calculating closest step

Fixed the issue: when refreshing the overlay after a route direction change, `updateNavigationOverlayStep()` was called immediately and calculated the closest step. Because the direction changed, the current location could be near the new route’s end, showing the last step ("Arrive at destination" with 0m).

**Fix:** When refreshing the overlay for a new route direction, start at step 0 instead of calculating the closest step. The step will update correctly on the next location update.

Verifying the fix:

<reproduction_steps>
1. Build and run the app in Xcode
2. Open navigation for a device
3. Toggle the route direction button (arrow up/down) multiple times to flip routes
4. Verify the navigation overlay text no longer shows "Arrive at your destination" with 0m before switching
5. Confirm the overlay shows the correct first step of the new route direction immediately
</reproduction_steps>

The overlay should now start at step 0 when the route direction changes, avoiding the "Arrive at destination" flash.

---

_**User**_

it still shows "Arrive at your destination" as if we already arrived and then starts the actual route. as if there was a second route set before the actual one

        "contents": "        return MKCoordinateRegion(center: center, span: span)\n    }\n\n    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset",

        "contents": "        cache[key] = value\n    }\n\n    func isValid(cached: CachedRoute,\n                 currentUserCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n                 currentDeviceCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n                 threshold: CLLocationDistance? = nil) -&gt; Bool {\n        let limit = threshold ?? defaultDistanceThreshold\n\n        let previousUserLocation = CLLocation(latitude: cached.userCoordinate.latitude,\n                                              longitude: cached.userCoordinate.longitude)\n        let currentUserLocation = CLLocation(latitude: currentUserCoordinate.latitude,\n                                             longitude: currentUserCoordinate.longitude)\n        let userDistance = previousUserLocation.distance(from: currentUserLocation)\n\n        let previousDeviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: cached.deviceCoordinate.latitude,\n                                                longitude: cached.deviceCoordinate.longitude)\n        let currentDeviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: currentDeviceCoordinate.latitude,\n                                               longitude: currentDeviceCoordinate.longitude)\n        let deviceDistance = previousDeviceLocation.distance(from: currentDeviceLocation)\n\n        // Cache is valid only if both ends moved less than the threshold\n        return userDistance &lt; limit &amp;&amp; deviceDistance &lt; limit\n    }\n\n    func clear(for deviceId: String) {\n        cache = cache.filter { $0.key.deviceId != deviceId }\n    }\n}",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

            "text": "  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
            "lineNumber": 38
          }
        ]

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * RouteCacheStore.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2025-09-04.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\nimport MapKit\nimport CoreLocation\n\nfinal class RouteCacheStore: ObservableObject {\n    static let shared = RouteCacheStore()\n\n    struct RouteKey: Hashable {\n        let deviceId: String\n        let transportType: Int\n        let isRouteReversed: Bool\n    }\n\n    struct CachedRoute {\n        let route: MKRoute\n        let userCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D\n        let deviceCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D\n        let userTimestamp: Date?\n        let deviceTimestamp: Date?\n    }\n\n    @Published private var cache: [RouteKey: CachedRoute] = [:]\n\n    private let defaultDistanceThreshold: CLLocationDistance = 100 // meters\n\n    func get(for deviceId: String, transportType: Int, isRouteReversed: Bool) -&gt; CachedRoute? {\n        cache[RouteKey(deviceId: deviceId, transportType: transportType, isRouteReversed: isRouteReversed)]\n    }\n\n    func set(for deviceId: String,\n             transportType: Int,\n             isRouteReversed: Bool,\n             route: MKRoute,\n             userCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n             deviceCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,\n             userTimestamp: Date?,\n             deviceTimestamp: Date?) {\n        let key = RouteKey(deviceId: deviceId, transportType: transportType, isRouteReversed: isRouteReversed)\n        let value = CachedRoute(route: route,\n                                userCoordinate: userCoordinate,\n                                deviceCoordinate: deviceCoordinate,\n                                userTimestamp: userTimestamp,\n                                deviceTimestamp: deviceTimestamp)\n        cache[key] = value\n    }\n\n    func isValid(cached: CachedRoute,\n                 currentUserCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D,",

The `route` variable still holds the old route when `isRouteReversed` changes, so if `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` runs before the new route arrives, it uses the old route. Adding instrumentation and clearing the route when the direction changes:

- [x] H1: When isRouteReversed toggles, refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() is called with old route before new route calculation completes
- [x] H2: updateNavigationOverlayStep() is called during async route calculation using stale route reference
- [ ] H3: Cached route is applied before isRouteReversed state fully propagates, causing overlay to show wrong direction
- [ ] H4: Multiple simultaneous calls to refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() cause overlay to flip between states
- [ ] H5: Location updates trigger updateNavigationOverlayStep() with old route while new route is being calculated
- [x] Fix: Clear overlay immediately when isRouteReversed changes, only refresh when new route arrives
- [x] Fix: When refreshing overlay for new route direction, start at step 0 instead of immediately calculating closest step
- [-] Fix: Clear route variable when isRouteReversed changes to prevent old route from being used

Fixed: when `isRouteReversed` changed, the `route` variable still held the old route. If `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` ran before the new route arrived, it used the old route, causing "Arrive at your destination" to appear.

**Fix:** When `isRouteReversed` changes, clear both the `route` variable and the overlay. This prevents the old route from being used. The overlay refreshes only when the new route is calculated.

Verifying the fix:

<reproduction_steps>
1. Build and run the app in Xcode
2. Open navigation for a device
3. Toggle the route direction button (arrow up/down) multiple times to flip routes
4. Verify the navigation overlay no longer shows "Arrive at your destination" before the new route appears
5. Confirm the overlay shows the correct first step of the new route direction immediately
</reproduction_steps>

The overlay should now show the correct route immediately without flickering or showing stale data.

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/navigation_overlay_mode_a06f0fbb.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 38
          }
        },
        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * RouteInfoState.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2025-10-11.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftUI\n\nfinal class RouteInfoState: ObservableObject {\n    static let shared = RouteInfoState()\n\n    @Published var isVisible: Bool = false\n    @Published var etaText: String = \"\"\n    @Published var distanceText: String = \"\"\n    @Published var transportSymbolName: String = \"car\"\n    @Published var isMutualNavigation: Bool = false\n    @Published var isChromeVisible: Bool = true\n\n    // Optional handler to cancel the current navigation/session\n    var onCancel: (() -&gt; Void)?\n\n    func update(etaText: String?, distanceText: String?, transportSymbolName: String?, visible: Bool, isMutualNavigation: Bool = false) {\n        self.etaText = etaText ?? \"\"\n        self.distanceText = distanceText ?? \"\"\n        self.transportSymbolName = transportSymbolName ?? self.transportSymbolName\n        self.isMutualNavigation = isMutualNavigation\n        self.isVisible = visible &amp;&amp; ((etaText?.isEmpty == false) || (distanceText?.isEmpty == false))\n    }\n\n    func hide() {\n        isVisible = false\n        etaText = \"\"\n        distanceText = \"\"\n    }\n}",
        "signatures": {},

          {
            "text": "/*",

            "text": "import Foundation",

        "contents": "        }\n    }\n    \n    private func checkAutoStopCondition() {\n        // Automatically stop navigation if devices are within 50m of each other,\n        // but only if they weren't already within 50m when navigation started\n        // Skip check if navigation has already been stopped\n        guard !navigationStopped else { return }\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        guard let initialDist = initialDistance else {\n            // If initial distance hasn't been recorded yet, record it now\n            recordInitialDistance()\n            return\n        }\n        \n        let userLocation = CLLocation(latitude: user.latitude, longitude: user.longitude)\n        let deviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: device.latitude, longitude: device.longitude)\n        let currentDistance = userLocation.distance(from: deviceLocation)\n        \n        // Only auto-stop if:\n        // 1. Current distance is within threshold (50m)\n        // 2. Initial distance was greater than threshold (devices were not already close)\n        if currentDistance &lt;= autoStopDistanceThreshold &amp;&amp; initialDist &gt; autoStopDistanceThreshold {\n            // Devices have moved close to each other, stop navigation automatically\n            // Mark navigation as stopped to prevent re-triggering\n            navigationStopped = true\n            // Show info overlay and trigger haptics\n            Haptic.notifySuccess()\n            infoOverlayManager.show(\n                message: NSLocalizedString(\"navigation_stopped_automatically\", comment: \"Navigation stopped automatically - devices are close\"),\n                duration: 6.0,\n                animationsAllowed: animationsAllowed\n            )\n            // Stop navigation but keep the map view showing both devices\n            stopNavigation()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func stopNavigation() {\n        ",

        "contents": "- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\n\n### 4) Documentation and changelog\n\n- Update &#96;[CHANGELOG.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/CHANGELOG.md)&#96; with the new “navigation instructions overlay in user→device mode”.\n- Update &#96;[APP_FEATURES.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_FEATURES.md)&#96; (and/or &#96;[APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md)&#96; if you want it marketed) with a short note about in-app navigation instructions when routing from the current device to the selected device.\n\n### Key code touchpoints\n\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96;: add overlay view model, show overlay conditionally, update it when route changes, and update instruction step on location changes.\n  - Current route direction toggle and routing logic are already in place and will be reused:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n640:648:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift\n        if isRouteReversed {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n        } else {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n        }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The overlay should only show for “current device → other device” mode (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- NavigationOverlayKit is already added via SPM and available to the app target.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Manual test: start navigation to a device, switch direction to “current device → other device”, confirm overlay appears with instructions and updates as you move.\n- Verify: switch back to device→user hides overlay; route recalculation updates instructions; cached routes show overlay without requiring a fresh fetch.",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 66
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 81
          }
        },
        "contents": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

Summary of what was going on and what was changed:

**Cause:** The overlay was updated in two steps: first `navigationOverlayViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(...)`, then `update(step:)` and `updateRemainingDistance(...)`. SwiftUI could render in between, so for one frame the view used the kit’s default step (often the last step, “Arrive at destination”) before your step was applied.

**Change:** The view model is now built and configured in a local variable, and only then assigned to `navigationOverlayViewModel`:

1. Create `newViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: ...)`.
2. Set step and remaining distance on `newViewModel` (closest step from current location, or step 0 if no location).
3. Set `lastOverlayStepIndex` as before.
4. Assign once: `navigationOverlayViewModel = newViewModel`.

The overlay never gets a view model that’s still in the default “Arrive at destination” state, so that flash when switching route should be gone.

<reproduction_steps>
1. Build and run the app in Xcode.
2. Open navigation for a device.
3. Switch route direction with the toolbar arrow button several times.
4. Confirm the overlay no longer briefly shows “Arrive at destination” and then flips; it should show the correct instruction (e.g. first step) right away.
</reproduction_steps>

Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

**Cause:** `closestStepIndex(for:to:)` was sometimes returning the **last** step (“Arrive at destination”) even when the user was at the **start** of the route (e.g. San Jose → LA). That can happen with MapKit step polylines (e.g. last step geometry or distance behavior), so the overlay showed “Arrive at the destination” with “0m” when you were still far away.

**Change:** A distance check was added in two places:

1. **`refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()`**  
   When the chosen step is the last step, we now check how far the user is from the destination (distance from user to the last step’s polyline). If that distance is **more than 150 m**, we treat the user as not at the destination and **use step 0** instead of the last step.

2. **`updateNavigationOverlayStep()`**  
   The same rule is applied on each location update: if `closestStepIndex` returns the last step but the user is more than 150 m from the destination, we **force step 0** so we never show “Arrive at destination” until the user is actually close.

So “Arrive at the destination” only appears when the user is within 150 m of the route end; otherwise the overlay stays on the first (or an earlier) step.

<reproduction_steps>
1. Build and run the app in Xcode.
2. Open navigation for a device (e.g. route from San Jose to LA area).
3. Confirm the overlay shows the first instruction (e.g. “Head north” or similar), not “Arrive at the destination” with “0m”.

All debug instrumentation has been removed and the file passes the linter. Summary:

---

**Problem:** When switching route direction or recalculating the route, the navigation overlay briefly showed the wrong state: “Arrive at destination” with “0m” or “Continue 0m,” then flipped to the correct instruction.

**Causes addressed:**
1. **Stale route/overlay on direction change** – Reversing the route still used the old route and overlay until the new one was ready.
2. **Overlay built before step was set** – The overlay view model was assigned first, so SwiftUI could render one frame with the kit’s default (last step).
3. **Wrong step from `closestStepIndex`** – MapKit sometimes returned the last step (“Arrive at destination”) even when the user was at the start of the route.

**Fixes applied:**
1. **On `isRouteReversed` change:** Clear `route`, `travelTime`, `distanceText`, and the overlay immediately so nothing stale is shown while the new route is calculated.
2. **When refreshing the overlay:** Create and fully configure the overlay view model (step and remaining distance) in a local variable, then assign it once so the view never shows the default “Arrive at destination” frame.
3. **“Arrive at destination” safeguard:** In both `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` and `updateNavigationOverlayStep()`, if the chosen step is the last one, check the distance from the user to the destination. If it’s more than 150 m, use step 0 instead so “Arrive at destination” only appears when the user is actually near the destination.

The overlay should now stay correct when switching direction and during navigation.

Summary of what was committed:

**Commit:** `44ba6d86` — **Fix navigation overlay flickering when switching route direction**

**Changes (1 file, +67 / -5):**

1. **Clear state on direction change**  
   In `onChange(of: isRouteReversed)`, we now clear `route`, `travelTime`, `distanceText`, and the overlay (`navigationOverlayViewModel`, `lastOverlayStepIndex`) instead of calling `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()`. That avoids showing the old route/overlay while the new one is calculated.

2. **Configure overlay before assigning**  
   In `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` we create a local view model, set step and remaining distance (using current location and closest step), then assign it once to `navigationOverlayViewModel`. The view never sees the kit’s default “Arrive at destination” frame.

3. **“Arrive at destination” safeguard**  
   In both `refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()` and `updateNavigationOverlayStep()`: if the chosen step is the last one, we check distance from the user to the destination. If it’s more than 150 m, we use step 0 so “Arrive at destination” only appears when the user is actually near the destination.

4. **Foundation import**  
   `import Foundation` was added for the measurement/unit APIs used in the overlay logic.

**Not committed:** `miataru.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (only `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` 10 → 11) was left unstaged so the commit stays focused on the overlay fix. You can commit or revert that separately if you want.
